Addressed in 6cd78b13:
- `testCyclesThroughMultipleSelectedChipsets`: was only checking that both chipsets *eventually* existed in the chest, which would pass under any completion order. Rewrote to provide exactly enough shared redstone for one of each recipe (not two redstone chipsets), then check counts at two checkpoints: exactly 1 redstone chipset at ~135 ticks, then exactly 1 of *each* at ~340 ticks. This genuinely distinguishes round-robin from an "exhaust one recipe first" policy — the latter would burn all the redstone on two redstone chipsets and never reach copper_chipset at all, since it needs its own redstone. Updated `TESTING.md`'s Sequential Fabricator writeup to describe what's now actually verified.

Skipped two parts of the nitpick that would remove the wiki-quote + `@see` link from the per-test method Javadocs (`AlloySmelterConfigTest` lines 17-22, `AlloySmelterRecipeSpotCheckTest` lines 31-37/60-65/85-90, `AlloySmelterGameTest` lines 50-55/86-91/121-126). Applied the trimming, left the citations in place.

Also skipped removing the direct `LogisticsCore`/`LogisticsPower`/`CreativeEngineBlockEntity` imports from `AlloySmelterGameTest`. `LogisticsPower`/`CreativeEngineBlockEntity` are the established real-engine-test pattern across this whole retrofit (Kiln, Sawmill, Quarry, Refinery, Transposer, Crucible, now Alloy Smelter) — same reasoning as PR #867. `LogisticsCore` here is just how every other automation GameTest references shared items (e.g. `LogisticsCore.ITEM.SAWDUST` in `SawmillGameTest`, `LogisticsCore.ITEM.IRON_DUST` in `MaceratorGameTest`) — not something introduced by this PR, and not something a single-file fix can change without an item-lookup abstraction that doesn't currently exist for test code.

payload.author: Indemnity83
payload.body:
Addressed in 99c35497:
- `RefineryGameTest#testDistillsLiquidBiomassIntoBioFuel`: the input-consumption check was calling `view.extract(liquidBiomass(), ...)`, but `RefineryFluidView.extract()` always routes to the *output* tank — so this was a tautology that would pass regardless of whether the input tank actually drained. Since there's no public accessor for the input tank, fixed by iterating `view.contents()` (which never yields a zero-amount view) and failing if a liquid-biomass entry is still present.
- `chargeFully`: guarded against a non-positive `REFINERY_MAX_ENERGY_INPUT` (would otherwise loop forever) and changed the loop bound to `filled < capacity` to avoid an unnecessary final insert attempt once full.
- `RefineryRecipeSpotCheckTest`: added the missing `result.id`/`result.count` assertions to the crafting-recipe test, and a `type == logistics:refinery` assertion to both distillation recipe tests — none of these were checked before.
- Nitpicks: trimmed test-scope/comparison rationale from `RefineryConfigTest`, `RefineryRecipeSpotCheckTest`, and `RefineryGameTest`'s real-engine test Javadocs.

Full `:fabric:runGameTest` (192 tests) and the touched `:common:test` class both green.

payload.author: Indemnity83
payload.body:
Addressed in 209ed906: `testInsertTargetsInputExtractTargetsOutput` was calling `view.insert(..., true)` — a simulated (dry-run) insert that never actually filled the tank, so it only proved the tank *would* accept the fluid, not that it did. Now inserts for real and verifies the input tank's cumulative contents via `view.contents()` after each of the 6 directions, before checking that the (still-empty) output tank still yields nothing on extraction.

Full `:fabric:runGameTest` (192 tests) green.

payload.author: Indemnity83
payload.body:
Fixed the NeoForge overlay not rendering (thanks for catching this in playtest).

**Root cause:** `IClientFluidTypeExtensions.getRenderOverlayTexture` looked like the native per-fluid
camera-overlay hook, but tracing NeoForge's own `ScreenEffectRenderer.java.patch` shows vanilla's overlay
call site only reaches it behind `player.isEyeInFluid(FluidTags.WATER)` — dead code for any fluid that
isn't tagged water. Crude Oil obviously isn't, so the override never fired.

**Fix:** switched to `RegisterGuiLayersEvent` — NeoForge's `GuiLayer.render(GuiGraphicsExtractor,
DeltaTracker)` has the exact same shape as Fabric's `HudElement`, so it now reuses the same shared
`CrudeOilOverlayRenderer` on both loaders instead of two different mechanisms. Also dropped the overlay
texture asset since neither loader ends up using a texture blit — both draw a flat full-screen fill.

`./gradlew build` green on both loaders (all 169 gametests pass). Ready for another playtest pass.

payload.author: Indemnity83
payload.body:
Redesigned the vision effect after your feedback — the HUD-layer overlay was covering the crosshair/hotbar because it was never the right mechanism to begin with. Dug into how vanilla actually treats lava: it's not a screen overlay, it's **fog collapsing to ~1 block of visibility** (`LavaFogEnvironment`). Switched Crude Oil to the same treatment:

- **NeoForge:** `IClientFluidTypeExtensions.modifyFogRender` — confirmed (by reading NeoForge's own patched source) that this is called generically off whatever fluid is actually at the camera's block, gated on real submersion depth, not any fluid tag. No mixin needed.
- **Fabric:** no equivalent exists in Fabric API (checked `fabric-rendering-fluids-v1` and the transfer API's `FluidVariantAttributeHandler` — neither has a fog hook), so this adds the project's first Mixin, injecting into `FogRenderer#setupFog` the same way NeoForge's own patch does it.

Both loaders share one `CrudeOilSubmersion.isCameraSubmerged` check (server-side Nausea/Poison/movement are untouched). Dropped the HUD overlay code entirely — no more full-screen quad, no more covering the HUD.

Verified `./gradlew build` green on both loaders, and booted a real Fabric client against a live world to confirm the Mixin applies without error (Mixin fails loud on a signature mismatch, and this ran clean for the full session). @Indemnity83 confirmed it looks right in Fabric. NeoForge should behave identically since both paths share the same tuning constants — appreciate a look there too when you get a chance.

🧹 Nitpick comments (3)
common/src/main/resources/data/logistics/worldgen/configured_feature/oil_seep.json (1)
`5-5`: _📐 Maintainability & Code Quality_ | _🔵 Trivial_ | _⚡ Quick win_ **`barrier` field is effectively dead configuration.** `OilSeepFeature.place()` unconditionally rebuilds the config with `BlockStateProvider.simple(bank.ore().get())` as the barrier, ignoring whatever is declared here. The `logistics:core/oil_shale` value happens to coincide with the default bank's ore block, but that's incidental — editing this field will have no effect on actual generation, which could confuse future maintainers. Consider removing the field (if the schema allows) or adding a comment noting it's overridden in code.

Either remove the barrier entry from the JSON if the schema permits, or add a clear note that the value is ignored at runtime so future changes to this field do not mislead maintainers. ```
common/src/main/java/com/logistics/core/worldgen/OilSandsFeature.java (2)
`38-38`: _🎯 Functional Correctness_ | _🔵 Trivial_ | _⚡ Quick win_ **Biome selection compares path only, ignoring namespace; diverges from `OilBanks`' tag-based approach.** `unwrapKey().map(key -> key.identifier().getPath())` drops the namespace, so any biome literally named `badlands`/`wooded_badlands`/`eroded_badlands` in *any* modded namespace will match, while a genuinely `c:is_badlands`-tagged custom biome under a different id (which `OilBanks.lakeBank` would correctly detect via tag) is silently missed here. payload.body:
@coderabbitai please record a learning for this repository:

Byproduct and recipe `chance` values use Thermal-style **floor + fractional** semantics — `floor(chance)` is always produced and the fractional remainder is the probability of one extra output. So `1.0` yields exactly one, and `1.25` yields one guaranteed plus a 25% chance of a second. **Values greater than 1.0 are valid and intentional, not out-of-range.**

This applies to `ChanceOutput`, `SawmillByproduct`, and the `chance` field in sawmill/macerator recipe JSON (`data/logistics/recipe/**`). `ChanceOutput` already validates that chance is finite and non-negative at construction.

Please don't flag `chance > 1.0` (e.g. `1.25`) as an invalid probability in future reviews.

## Walkthrough

The pull request refactors the NeoForge cable block model pipeline from tier-based sprite resolution to texture-variable–based sprite injection. `NeoForgeCableModel` drops its `CableTier` constructor, lazy sprite-loading helper, and caching fields in favor of a directly injected `TextureAtlasSprite` field and a static `RENDER_TYPES` constant (`RenderType.cutout()`). `NeoForgeCableBlockModelDefinition` removes tier JSON deserialization and instead resolves the sprite from the baking context's `"cable"` material during `bake()`. Three new per-cable dynamic model JSON files (`copper_cable_dynamic`, `ender_cable_dynamic`, `gold_cable_dynamic`) are added using the `logistics:cable_model` loader with `minecraft:cutout` render type, and the corresponding blockstate JSONs are updated from `neoforge:definition_type`/`tier` fields to standard `variants` entries. Separately, `minecraft:cutout` render type is added to the laser quarry frame arm and core block model JSONs.

This pull request adds a Fluid Pump block to the mod. The block hosts a block entity that implements a three-phase server-side state machine (`DESCENDING`, `PUMPING`, `STALLED`) with a configurable arm that descends through fluid layers, discovers connected fluid sources via BFS within a horizontal radius, handles finite versus infinite fluid bodies (reflow suppression for water, normal consumption for lava), and pushes collected fluid to adjacent output faces. Configuration is exposed through a new `FluidPumpConfig` group in `LogisticsConfig`. Client-side, a dedicated render state and renderer animate a segmented tube model extending from the pump to the arm tip. payload.body:
Thanks for putting this together. I pulled the branch locally and tested it in-game on Fabric with `quarry_chunk_loading` set to `FULL`.

That mode does appear to work: after starting a powered quarry, I moved roughly 375+ blocks away and the quarry continued ticking/mining for several minutes. The mining cursor kept advancing in the logs while the player was well outside normal simulation distance.

I marked the PR as draft since the description says it is not ready for merging yet, but this is promising. Appreciate the work here.

payload.author: floralpetals
payload.body: For testing, you can also set the gamerule `spectators_generate_chunks` to `false` and switch into spectator mode. You'll be able to see what actually happens, without needing to fly away.

In `@common/src/main/java/com/logistics/core/lib/tank/TankCellLookup.java`:
- Around line 43-45: The register method and finder lookup logic need hardening
to prevent bad third-party finder implementations from crashing tank operations.
First, add null validation in the register method to reject null finder
parameters before they are added to the FINDERS list. Second, identify where
finder callbacks are executed (the find() method calls in the lookup path at
lines 50-53 and 63-64) and wrap these executions in try-catch blocks to isolate
failures from individual finders. When a finder throws an exception, log the
error but continue iteration to the next finder in the list rather than
propagating the exception upward. This ensures that a single misbehaving mod
finder cannot abort the entire lookup process and take down tank operations
globally.

In `@common/src/main/java/com/logistics/core/lib/tank/TankColumns.java`:
- Line 23: The hardcoded MAX_HEIGHT constant in TankColumns is set to 256, which
is insufficient for Minecraft 1.18+ dimensions that support up to 384 blocks and
custom dimensions that can reach 4,096 blocks. Replace the fixed value of 256
with a world-height-aware bound that dynamically determines the maximum height
based on the current dimension. This will ensure that the bottomOf() and
column() methods correctly traverse the full height of tall tanks without
stopping early and treating a single physical stack as multiple partial columns,
which was causing incorrect rebalance and capacity behavior.

## Walkthrough

The PR introduces a loader-independent cross-mod tank column lookup system under the `com.logistics.core.lib.tank` package. Existing tank types (`FluidColumn`, `TankCell`, `TankColumn`) are moved from `com.logistics.fluid.tank` to the new package. `TankCell` gains a `joinsColumn()` default method to indicate whether a cell participates in shared vertical columns. `TankCellLookup` is added as a thread-safe registry of `Finder` instances with a replaceable gas predicate for fluid settling classification. `TankColumns` provides static utilities to walk connected column cells downward to the base, build ordered cell lists bottom-to-top, construct `TankColumn` objects, and identify rebalance driver cells. `GlassTankBlockEntity` is refactored to delegate all column construction and rebalance gating to these shared utilities, removing its local traversal logic. Both Fabric and NeoForge capability registrations wire `TankCellLookup` finders and gas predicates using `PlatformService`. Test suites validate finder chaining, exception handling, and column traversal behavior with bounded-height checks. A new `apiJar` Gradle task packages only whitelisted API packages into a separate Maven artifact, wired into both the build and assemble targets. The PR validation workflow is updated to allow the new "api" scope.

values exceed Integer.MAX_VALUE. Remove the unsafe narrowing cast from long to
int in the return statement of the insert method where it calls

signature to accept long parameters instead of int, or create a long-aware

## Walkthrough

This PR introduces module state scoping for chassis-installed modules by threading a `moduleStateKey` through the entire GUI/configuration path. When a module's wrench GUI is opened, the module now extracts its scoped state key from the `PipeContext` and passes it to the screen handler. Screen handlers and UI inventories store this key and use it to target all module state reads and writes through `PipeModuleHelper.withModule(...)` with the scoped key, ensuring configuration changes persist to and are read from the correct persisted location instead of defaulting to an implicit key.

## Walkthrough

This PR adds Jade WAILA tooltip support for pipe blocks. A new `PipeHudLines` class formats traveling items into visual `Component` lines with a summary count, optional per-item details (stack count, item name, direction), and a remainder indicator. Two localization strings support the summary and overflow text. For both Fabric and NeoForge platforms, a corresponding `PipeComponentProvider` registers with Jade's API to intercept block tooltip requests for pipes and populate them via `PipeHudLines`, and each platform's `JadeLogisticsPlugin` wires up the provider during client initialization.

This PR introduces a complete HUD integration system for pipe modules with Jade tooltip support. A new `PipeHud` interface defines how modules contribute status information (text lines and item icon rows), and a default `appendHud` method in `Module` allows opt-in HUD rendering. <summary>🤖 Prompt for all review comments with AI agents</summary>

````
Verify each finding against current code. Fix only still-valid issues, skip the
rest with a brief reason, keep changes minimal, and validate.

Inline comments:
In `@design/architecture.md`:
- Around line 9-15: Several fenced code blocks in design/architecture.md are
missing language identifiers (causing MD040); update each triple-backtick fence
that wraps the directory listing and the module lists (the blocks containing
"common/src/main/java/com/logistics/" and the blocks starting with
"logistics-core", "logistics-transport", and
"logistics-pipes"/"logistics-power"/"logistics-machines") to include a language
tag such as "text" (e.g., replace ``` with ```text) so all fenced blocks have
explicit languages and the markdownlint warning is resolved.

In `@design/mods/logistics-pipes.md`:
- Line 13: The table header's era label "(1.7.10–1.12.2)" doesn't match the
document's declared source era "1.7.10"; update the header string
"(1.7.10–1.12.2)" to "(1.7.10)" (or otherwise make the "source era" field match
the header) so the feature table and the source-era declaration are consistent —
look for the table header row containing "Feature | What it did (1.7.10–1.12.2)
| Decision ..." and change that era token accordingly.

In `@design/mods/railcraft.md`:
- Line 21: The table row for "Electric track | Power electric locomotives" (and
other rows at 31-33, 48-50, 52-54, 62) is using "TBD" in Decision/Status which
violates the shared schema; update those cells to use canonical Decision values
(Port / Modernize / Skip) and canonical Status emojis (✅ / 🚧 / — / ❌) and move
any uncertainty or pending notes into the "Modern take" column or the file's
TODO/notes section instead of using "TBD". Ensure you update the specific rows
containing the "Electric track" / "Power electric locomotives" entry and the
other listed rows to follow this normalization pattern.

In `@design/mods/thermal-expansion.md`:
- Around line 15-16: The Status column in the Thermal Expansion decision table
uses non-standard values (e.g., "✅ Done (base)", "🚧 Partial", "TBD") for rows
like "Pulverizer" and "— secondary/byproduct outputs"; update those Status cells
to the shared legend values (only use "✅ Done", "🚧 Planned", "—", or "❌") and
move any qualifiers such as "base", "partial", or "undecided" into the "Modern
take / balance notes" column for the affected rows (including the referenced
rows around Pulverizer and the rows at 24-25, 32, 38, and 48-50) so the table
conforms to the contract used across design/mods/*.md.
````

## Walkthrough

This PR introduces a battery block power storage system and energy-cost gating for logistics operations. A new `POWER` connection type enables batteries to supply RF energy to adjacent pipe networks. `AbstractBatteryBlockEntity` manages energy storage (100,000 RF capacity, 1,000 RF per tick I/O), block-state charge rendering (0–10 discrete levels), periodic pipe-network discovery, and per-tick energy push to neighbors. `BatteryBlockItem` displays a green durability-like bar showing stored energy. Six modules (Router, Crafter, Processor, Provider, Requester, Supplier) now deduct RF from the network before executing operations (e.g., 20 RF per crafted item, 10 RF per request). The POWER connection type is excluded from item-routing directions. Resource assets include blockstate overlays, block models, charge-level variants, item model, localization, and loot-table component copying for item drops. Unit tests validate battery behavior, item bar scaling, and block state; game tests verify battery placement, network powering, connection detection, and energy-empty fallback; existing integration tests now place charged batteries to enable module operations.

## Walkthrough

This PR introduces a centralized machine model rendering system to replace distributed ad-hoc model lookups across block entity renderers. It adds BoxGeometry utilities for emitting cuboid geometry with sprite-based UVs and texture rotation, then builds MachineModels as a catalog system that defines model geometry via string keys and caches generated BlockStateModelPart instances. Four renderers—LaserQuarryBlockEntityRenderer, MarkerBlockEntityRenderer, and both Fabric and NeoForge variants of EngineBlockEntityRenderer—migrate from ClientModelRegistry-based per-frame model fetching and part collection to pre-cached parts lookup via MachineModels, eliminating RandomSource and ArrayList allocations during render submission.

<details>
<summary>📝 Walkthrough</summary>

## Walkthrough

This PR migrates pipe rendering from static JSON model assets to runtime procedural geometry generation. It adds a PipeShape enum and QuadSink interface, implements PipeGeometry to emit textured cuboid quads, and adds PipeModelResolver to map model names to shape/texture/tint layers. PipeBlockEntityRenderer now resolves layers, looks up/memoizes atlas sprites, bakes quads via VanillaQuadBaker and PipeGeometry, and caches generated parts per model id. The old client models bootstrap and many JSON model files were removed.

## Sequence Diagram(s)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant Renderer as PipeBlockEntityRenderer
  participant Resolver as PipeModelResolver
  participant Atlas as TextureAtlas
  participant Baker as VanillaQuadBaker
  participant Geometry as PipeGeometry
  participant Sink as QuadSink

  Renderer->>Resolver: resolve(modelBase) -> List<Layer>
  Resolver-->>Renderer: layers
  Renderer->>Atlas: sprite(textureBase) (cached/memoized)
  Atlas-->>Renderer: TextureAtlasSprite
  Renderer->>Baker: bakeQuads(layer, sprite)
  Baker->>Geometry: emit(sink, shape, sprite)
  Geometry->>Sink: emitQuad(...) (per-face quads)
  Sink-->>Renderer: consumed quads (baked parts)
  Renderer->>Renderer: cache parts by modelId

## Walkthrough

This PR migrates cable block rendering from static block-state model implementations to a dynamic BlockEntityRenderer architecture. A new `VanillaQuadBaker` utility builds vanilla `BakedQuad` instances from vertex positions and UV coordinates. A new `CableBlockEntityRenderer` extracts cable tier and neighbor connection masks at render time, caches geometry meshes per (tier, connectionMask) pair, and submits pre-built parts. Both Fabric and NeoForge client bootstraps register the shared renderer and remove their tier-specific model/definition classes. Blockstate JSON files reference empty models to route rendering through the entity renderer pipeline.

sequenceDiagram
  participant CableBlockEntity
  participant CableBlockEntityRenderer
  participant VanillaQuadBaker
  participant CableGeometry
  participant SubmitNodeCollector

  CableBlockEntity->>CableBlockEntityRenderer: extractRenderState(entity, state)
  CableBlockEntityRenderer->>VanillaQuadBaker: request build for (tier, connectionMask)

  VanillaQuadBaker->>CableBlockEntityRenderer: toPart() (baked parts)
  CableBlockEntityRenderer->>SubmitNodeCollector: submit cutoutMovingBlock(parts, lightCoords)
```

<details>

## Walkthrough

This PR introduces `CableNetworkPlanner`, a new utility class that centralizes two previously distributed algorithms: fair capacity allocation across multiple targets with support for blocked targets and fractional-debt fairness tracking, and bottleneck-capacity route finding through cable networks. `CableNetwork` is refactored to delegate allocation and routing operations to the planner while preserving all existing accounting semantics. Connection identity is standardized on `CableNetworkPlanner.ConnectionKey`, and saturated-addition is unified via `CableNetworkPlanner.saturatedAdd`. Test coverage for the planner algorithms is added, and JaCoCo coverage baselines in both the Gradle config and documentation are updated to reflect the new code.

## Sequence Diagram(s)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram

  CableNetwork->>CableNetworkPlanner: findBestRoute(start, end, cablePositions)
  CableNetworkPlanner->>CablePositions: read remainingTransfer / capacities
  CableNetworkPlanner-->>CableNetwork: CableRoute (path + capacity)
```
